title: Agent trajectories as programs: fingerprinting and programming coding-agent behavior
title_zh: 将 Agent 轨迹视为程序：编码 Agent 行为的指纹识别与编程
abstract_en: Benchmark scores tell you what an agent got right; they do not tell you how it got there. In this work, we introduce methods for comparing agents procedurally in different contexts, where the model, tasks, and approaches vary. We compare ten agents and find that they are identifiable by their behavioral habits, which we define as fingerprints: a probe over these procedural signatures attributes an unseen trajectory to the correct agent at 85.7% accuracy, controlling for leakage across tasks. We develop procedural representations for agent problem-solving procedures with an emergent vocabulary induction technique that is meant to be maximally compressive to avoid surface-level variation while being expressive enough to unveil the quirks of the models' patterns. We apply our framework to the software engineering evaluation dataset SWE-Bench to study the structural distinctness of agent trajectories and find that behavior is most similar between models from similar release periods and those that are distilled from one another (e.g., a distilled student model and its teacher have a Jensen-Shannon divergence of 0.25, about half the distance between other model pairs). As more models saturate evaluations, we believe that it will be important to probe model behavior along more holistic dimensions than success rates alone. We introduce ProcGrep, a library for auditing and evaluating agents for how they approach tasks at a procedural level given their traces in a top-down fashion. We believe this work has a range of applications to help developers work with and program coding agents, such as task-aware model routing, agent monitoring, and finer-grained cost analysis.
abstract_zh: 本文指出，传统 benchmark 分数只能说明 agent 做对了什么，却难以揭示其如何解决问题。作者提出一种从过程层面比较不同 coding agents 的方法，可在模型、任务和实现方式不同的情况下分析 agent 的行为轨迹。研究比较了 10 个 agents，发现它们具有可识别的行为习惯，即“指纹”：在控制任务泄漏后，一个基于过程签名的探针能以 85.7% 准确率将未见过的轨迹归因到正确 agent。论文提出一种用于表示 agent 解题过程的程序化表征方法，通过 emergent vocabulary induction 诱导出尽可能压缩、减少表层差异但仍能表达模型行为模式的词汇。作者在 SWE-Bench 软件工程评测数据集上应用该框架，研究 agent 轨迹的结构差异，发现发布时间相近的模型以及存在蒸馏关系的模型行为更相似，例如蒸馏学生模型与教师模型的 Jensen-Shannon divergence 为 0.25，约为其他模型对距离的一半。论文还发布 ProcGrep，一个用于自顶向下审计和评估 agent 过程行为的库，面向任务感知模型路由、agent 监控和更细粒度成本分析等应用。
key_points_zh: 提出将 agent trajectories 视为程序化过程签名，用于比较不同 coding agents 的解题方式，而不只看 benchmark 成功率。
在 10 个 agents 上验证行为“指纹”存在：基于过程签名的探针可用 85.7% 准确率识别未见轨迹所属 agent，并控制了跨任务泄漏。
通过 emergent vocabulary induction 构建压缩但有表达力的程序化表征，以弱化表层差异、突出模型特有的过程习惯。
在 SWE-Bench 上发现，发布时间相近或蒸馏相关的模型轨迹结构更相似；学生模型与教师模型的 Jensen-Shannon divergence 仅为 0.25。
发布 ProcGrep 库，用于从过程层面审计和评估 coding agents，可支持任务感知模型路由、agent 监控和细粒度成本分析。

llm_assessment.comment: This work adds valuable trace-level observability and behavioral auditing tools for coding agents, with plausible uses in routing and monitoring.
llm_assessment.comment_zh: 该工作提供了有价值的轨迹级可观测性和行为审计方法，可用于编码智能体的路由与监控。
